assessment: All 14 retained main-PDF pages were text-read and inspected as renders, with enlarged figures, tables and formulae. The review records two figures, four tables, the 13-row abbreviation list, two unnumbered printed identities, 26 numbered footnotes and 38 bibliography entries. Thirty-nine limited checks, 30 capacity cells, six historical classification cases, 12 reported credit-value cells, 24 finite-credit examples and three price-growth examples do not reproduce the native Table 4 model. No exact original citation passages were verified. Historical legal applicability, credit timing/release assumptions, source notation and missing native assets remain open; no accepted operating/GHG input changed.

sections.scope: Identity, abstract, keywords, affiliations and abbreviations
sections.assessment: Sven Bode and Martina Jung, International Environmental Agreements 6 (2006), 173–186. DOI 10.1007/s10784-006-9004-4. Received 10 August 2005, accepted 8 May 2006, online 8 July 2006. Springer copyright 2006; no CC licence identified. Read all 13 abbreviations and distinct capture, storage and buyer roles.

Read UNFCCC climate goals, source reduction versus atmospheric sinks, historical efficiency and renewable-policy discussion. The legal and deployment context is 2006, not a verified present-day framework.

Read capture including compression, transport, storage, three capture methods, 15–40% energy-output penalty, historical pipeline/ship context and three geological media. Generic duties and technology maturity statements are not a complete same-case utility inventory.

Read all 30 Table 1 intervals, regional allocation footnote, cost identity, avoided/captured denominator caveats, monetary EOR revenues and missing monitoring costs. Listed totals 476–5880 Gt close; 1660 Gt best estimate is not identified from bounds. Saline aquifers lack a Table 1 column.

Read site-specific retention, uncertain seepage, well integrity and earthquakes. Site screening is necessary but does not by itself ensure complete accounting or allocate liability. Figure 1 distinguishes energy-related and fugitive emissions.

Read Article 1.8 quotation and assumed point-source classification; authors explicitly call the choice political and unresolved at that time. Footnote 10 distinguishes biomass; the argument is not a universal classification of all CCS/CDR.

Read all six combinations and merged storage cells in Table 2, JI/domestic/CDM distinctions, inventory quality and third-country buyer caveats. Non-Annex participation alone does not imply CDM under the authors assumption.

Read bans, ex-ante discounting and monitored actual releases, moral-hazard discussion, HWP analogy, export-country accounting and temporary buyer liability. Table 3 contains conditional proposals rather than verified current treaty obligations.

Read replacement-cost definition, Vtemp=Vperm−RC, stable-price assumption, three discount/four release columns and limits of the near-negligible-value-loss conclusion. Missing release, payment, renewal and horizon conventions prevent exact native reproduction.

Read 21/60-year historical limits, alternative nonrenewable/renewable terms, credit expiry and missed economic benefits beyond expiry. No physical release at the credit boundary is established. Schematic release lines have unscaled time axes.

Read repeated conditional legal classification, proposed liability, literal (>0.01) without units, short-credit-period qualification and explicit multi-exporter/shared/transboundary reservoir limits. Do not correct the inequality or infer current national obligations.

All 38 printed entries read in text and renders with line/page geometry. Native Heafeli/Haefeli and Romberg/Rumberg spellings and Pearce report placeholders/year ambiguity preserved; exact originals remain unverified.

No embedded files or explicit SI/code/data availability section identified. Local absence does not prove online absence. No licence for unavailable external assets, author code or current legal instruments inferred; no author contacted.
Direct air capture proposals by Ha-Duong/Keith 2002 and Lackner 1999; a distinct atmospheric source pathway.
OECD/IEA2004 also identifies fuel extraction/transformation as capture sources.
Food/fertilizer utilization has short retention; not a durable-storage example.
Trucks and trains are also possible transport modes.
Historical EOR experience/profitability and limited EGR/ECBM maturity, not current universal economics.
Avoided-cost includes energy penalty and differs from captured-cost; eleven listed cost sources plus IPCC synthesis remain unverified.
Baseline plant choice is crucial to avoidance cost; Anderson/Newell original unverified.
Additional cited storage-cost studies and IPCC synthesis are not independent field service observations.
IPCC ranges 0–70 US$/t avoided for pulverized coal versus 20–270 with NGCC reference; baseline boundaries differ.
Biomass combustion must be treated differently from the assumed fossil point-source classification.
CDM credit generation depends on the subsequent accounting analysis, not a storage-only location flag.
A third Annex I buyer may participate in JI; capture country receives reduction accounting and may compensate the store.
Non-ratification and inadequate inventory quality can create similar accounting gaps.
Annex I restriction assumes Kyoto ratification and minimum inventory quality.
Yoshigahara et al.2004 is cited for default-factor/accounting methods; original unverified.
DTI quotation says credible discount rates are constrained by uncertain storage fluxes; Pearce monitoring review is separately cited.
Proposed release/refill incentive after permanent credit issuance is a moral-hazard hypothesis, not observed misconduct.
Heafeli/Haefeli 2004 pp 21–22 supports the inventory discussion only if the original passage is verified.
HWP production-approach analogy assigns exported-pool emissions to exporter; not a current CCS rule.
Authors consider permanent CERs with Annex I storage unproblematic in case 3, conditional on inventory accounting.
Temporary and long-term forestry CER types referenced; ambiguous l/I glyph and Rumberg/Romberg metadata not silently corrected.
Herzog/Caldeira/Reilly 2003 cited for temporary-storage effectiveness, not independently reproduced here.
Ha-Duong/Keith 2003 cited for replacement-cost context; no original formula check.
Temporary value is a chain of temporary credits during the crediting period; exact issuance/renewal timing omitted.
Increasing-price tendency is asserted; convergence and price-growth/discount relation must be specified before generalizing.
Historical alternatives: nonrenewable 10/30 years or 7/20 years with two renewals, yielding 21/60 maxima.

visuals.inspection: All 13 rows read: CCS, CDM, CER, ECBM, EOR, Former S.U., GHG, HWP, IPCC, JI, LULUCF, RC, UNFCCC. Definitions and institutional roles kept distinct.

All six on/offshore and Annex/non/total rows, five medium columns, 30 lower/upper interval cells, Gt units and footnote inspected enlarged. Saline aquifers discussed in prose but absent as a table column; former Soviet allocation ambiguous.

Inspected main capture→transport→injection/store and EOR recapture loop, all energy CO2e and fugitive CO2f labels, legend and source caption. It is a qualitative boundary diagram without native quantities, and does not close produced-oil combustion or whole LCA.
All six rows, merged storage Annex I cases 1–3/non Annex I cases 4–6 and mechanism footnote read enlarged. Native classification mechanically reconstructs; no proof of current legal applicability.

Four grouped rows cover all six cases; storing country for 1/2/3, capture country for 4, temporary-credit buyer for 5/6. Read footnote and permanent-CER distinction for 3. Proposed accounting party is not necessarily reservoir operator.

All 12 cells at discount 1/5/10% and release 0/.01/.1/1%, constant-price footnote read enlarged. Values preserved exactly. Two explicit analyst cash-flow timing conventions do not reconcile nonzero-release cells; missing native calculation remains open.

Read initial-input arrow, unscaled stored-carbon/time axes, release 0/1/5/10% lines, vertical end-of-credit marker, brackets and caption. Schematic lines do not identify original-stock versus remaining-stock release law or a measured retention profile.

equations.check: All components must share currency/year, service boundary and mass denominator. A sum of separately quoted avoided/captured/transported costs is not automatically valid.
RC is discounted future replacement spending; subtracting it from monetary value does not calculate retained physical mass. Full native RC expression and timing are not printed.

equations.printed: Analyst isolated-cohort law R_t=(1−lambda)^t and release_t=lambda*(1−lambda)^(t−1)
equations.check: Explicit remaining-stock fractional release assumption; native Table 4/Fig 2 release basis is unspecified. Not a fitted site law.
Uses an initial cohort, annual end-year replacement and price growthg. Under constant price, unrestricted RC/P0=lambda/(r+lambda). Neither timing convention is inferred to be native.

equations.printed: Analyst unrestricted temporary value/P0=r/(r+lambda), for constant price and r+lambda>0
equations.check: Year-end isolated-cohort diagnostic. Nine nonzero native cells remain outside nearest 0.1 percentage-point display rounding; not proof the authors model is erroneous.

equations.printed: Analyst year-start comparison RC_start=(1+r)*RC_end under constant price
equations.check: Moves each replacement one year earlier. Explicit alternative only; no native verification/renewal cycle established.

equations.printed: Analyst finite-expiry RC_T/P0=lambda*h*sum(a^k, k=0..T−1)+a^T, h=(1+g)/(1+r), a=(1−lambda)*h
equations.check: Terminal term replaces surviving credits atT while the mass may remain stored. Independent cash-flow sums check the geometric expression, includinga=1.
For constant price andlambda 0, physical retention stays 100% even when financial value is 18.86% at 1% discount/21 years. Expiry is not physical release.

equations.printed: Analyst convergence condition (1−lambda)*(1+g)/(1+r)<1 for positive release
equations.check: An increasing price path can reduce value or make unrestricted replacement PV diverge. Native footnote 25 supplies no path or parameter limits; no native growth calculation reproduced.

equations.printed: Analyst interval total and midpoint: low 476, high 5880, midpoint 3178 Gt
equations.check: Endpoint sums reproduce quoted range, but do not derive reported best 1660 or a probability median/mean.

equations.printed: Analyst mass ledger: retained=captured−downstream releases; avoided=baseline−uncaptured−utility emissions−downstream releases
equations.check: Disclosed 100 t baseline/90 captured/15 utility/2 transport loss/1 storage release gives 87 retained and 72 avoided. Utility carbon is distinct from fugitive original carbon.
Disclosed 2 currency/t at 90 t versus 72 t avoided becomes 2.5 currency/t avoided. No source cost or accepted input corrected.

variables.name: Listed geological resource
variables.assumption: Oil/gas/coal intervals; no pressure/rate history or explicit aquifer column. Endpoint covariance and best-estimate selection unknown.

variables.name: CCS and component costs
variables.assumption: Euro and US dollar source ranges not harmonized by year/baseline. Captured, transported, avoided and monitored mass differ.

variables.name: Energy penalty
variables.assumption: Gross/net/reference-output basis and compression allocation not sufficiently specified; not separate heat/electricity inventory.

variables.name: Capture, storage and buyer parties
variables.assumption: Tables 2/3 conditional 2006 policy framework; country group is not a safety or leakage distribution.

variables.name: Vtemp, Vperm, RC
variables.assumption: Vtemp+RC=Vperm; a financial fraction is not retained-carbon fraction.

variables.name: Release rate
variables.assumption: Table columns 0, .01, .1, 1% converted to 0, .0001, .001, .01 for analyst model only; original stock/time law unknown.

variables.name: Discount rate
variables.assumption: 1, 5, 10% financial discounting, not physical loss or climate decay.

variables.name: Carbon price and growth
variables.unit: constant price native; analyst P0=1,g per year
variables.assumption: No currency price or native path invented. Positive release and sufficiently high growth can invalidate infinite PV.

variables.name: Crediting period versus retention
variables.assumption: Historical 21/60 maxima and 10/30 alternatives; expiry does not imply a physical release or expiry of every broader liability.

variables.name: Energy-related versus fugitive CO2
variables.assumption: CO2e and CO2f are graphic labels for energy/fugitive CO2; do not read the former as a complete multi-gas CO2e inventory.

variables.name: Conclusion (>0.01)
variables.assumption: Greater-than sign and absence of percent preserved; no automatic less-than 0.01% retention assumption.

variables.name: Site integrity and liability
variables.assumption: Monitoring accuracy, default seepage, commingled sources and stock-dependent releases not quantitatively modeled.

claims.claim: CCS non-permanence and cross-border accounting require liability arrangements.
claims.assessment: Historical problem framing; source abatement and atmospheric removal kept distinct, not current legal determination.

claims.claim: Efficiency improvements/no-regret measures did not meet earlier expectations.
claims.assessment: Cited historical policy interpretation, not independently verified energy trend.

claims.claim: CCS comprises capture including compression, transport and storage.
claims.assessment: Useful boundary decomposition, but no complete matched utility inventory.

claims.claim: Post/pre-combustion and oxyfuel are principal large-point-source capture routes.
claims.assessment: Historical technology description, not reproduced capture model.

claims.claim: Energy penalty 15–40% and compression additional energy.
claims.assessment: Denominator and compression allocation require care; no GJ/t or k Wh/t pair established.

claims.claim: Industrial hydrogen/gas processing separates CO2; DAC also proposed.
claims.assessment: Vented/used/sequestered and atmospheric/fossil sources differ.

claims.claim: US pipeline length~2800 km and shipping favored over longer/water-separated routes.
claims.assessment: Historical infrastructure/economic context; no current universal ship/pipeline break-even.

claims.claim: Oil/gas, saline aquifers and coal seams offer storage; EOR/EGR/ECBM maturity differs.
claims.assessment: Historical market/technology categories, not current availability or net climate benefit.

claims.claim: Resource estimates are uncertain; quoted range 476–5880 Gt and best 1660 Gt.
claims.assessment: Five-column endpoints sum exactly; best estimate not derived from intervals. These are not annual pressure-safe capacities.

claims.claim: Saline aquifers more evenly distributed; non-Annex I countries hold larger share.
claims.assessment: No aquifer column in Table 1; Annex allocation and joint uncertainty need original Hendriks data. Endpoint majority is not universal interval dominance.

claims.claim: Full CCS cost includes capture, transport, storage and monitoring.
claims.assessment: Native sum requires common denominator, currency/year and scope; missing monitoring prevents a closed full-chain estimate.

claims.claim: Capture 24–52€/t avoided; ammonia/hydrogen lower.
claims.assessment: Historical reference-dependent cost, not capture utility or net-GHG factor.

claims.claim: Avoided cost includes energy penalty and exceeds captured cost under matched assumptions.
claims.assessment: Read all footnote 6 literature and baseline qualification; no universal cross-case ratio inferred.

claims.claim: Gas/coal reference investment strongly changes avoidance costs.
claims.assessment: Counterfactual plant matters; no native same-case baseline reproduced.

claims.claim: Pipeline 1–6€/t per 100 km, shipping cheaper at longer distances.
claims.assessment: Scale/state/terrain/regulation and route boundary matter; cannot linearize into a universal modern service cost.

claims.claim: Storage 1–11€/t and EOR−10 to 30 including oil revenue.
claims.assessment: Monetary revenue credits are not avoided climate emissions; source cost arrays and complete LCI absent.

claims.claim: Full combinations span−3 to 106€/t avoided with little monitoring-cost experience.
claims.assessment: Unspecified distance, capture variant, matched denominator and monitoring prevent exact reconstruction; no definite arithmetic-error claim.

claims.claim: IPCC coal and NGCC-reference avoided costs have different ranges.
claims.assessment: Footnote 9 gives 0–70 and 20–270 US$/t with distinct baselines; original SPM unverified.

claims.claim: Retention is site-specific; seepage and sudden releases uncertain.
claims.assessment: Geology/history/wells/seals and earthquakes discussed without calibrated leakage or pressure-service model.

claims.claim: Strict site selection necessary but insufficient for full GHG accounting.
claims.assessment: Physical suitability and accounting completeness are different requirements.

claims.claim: Figure 1 identifies energy and fugitive emissions across capture/transport/injection/storage/EOR recapture.
claims.assessment: Qualitative diagram only; no supplier/mass/electricity totals or produced-oil-use emissions.

claims.claim: Point-source CCS probably qualifies as source reduction under Article 1.8, assuming the authors framework.
claims.assessment: Explicit political/unresolved qualification and biomass exception preserved; no universal DAC/biomass/current-law claim.

claims.claim: Capture location determines Annex I mitigation versus CDM in all six cases.
claims.assessment: Mechanical reconstruction corroborates Tables 2/3. Case 4 has non-Annex storage without CDM under the assumed framework.

claims.claim: Annex I storage-country inventories cover seepage in cases 1–3.
claims.assessment: Requires ratification/inventory-quality assumptions; not current legal verification.

claims.claim: Storage in non-Annex I may leave no emission-budget deduction under then-current rules.
claims.assessment: Historical accounting gap, not a claim every such project has no present liability.

claims.claim: Options include storage ban, ex-ante discounting or monitored actual releases.
claims.assessment: Normative alternatives; no optimized policy selection or calibrated discount factor.

claims.claim: Credible standard seepage discount rates unavailable and shocks/wilful release problematic.
claims.assessment: 2006 source quotation and uncertainty; no measured failure probability supplied.

claims.claim: Permanent-credit release/refill could create incentives to repeat credit issuance.
claims.assessment: Hypothetical moral hazard, not evidence of observed conduct.

claims.claim: Exporting Annex I capture country could include non-Annex reservoir releases in its own inventory.
claims.assessment: Proposed case 4 accounting; HWP production approach is an analogy, not enacted CCS rule.

claims.claim: Temporary-credit buyers could retain liability in cases 5/6; case 3 can use permanent CER with Annex I storage inventory.
claims.assessment: Proposed instruments and parties are kept distinct from storage operators and current treaty obligations.

claims.claim: Economic comparisons must include replacement costs for non-permanence.
claims.assessment: Cited economic background, not verified native valuation or storage-effectiveness model.

claims.claim: RC is discounted permanent-credit purchases compensating future releases; Vtemp=Vperm−RC.
claims.assessment: Printed identity checked; source does not give full RC recurrence/payment timing. Financial value not physical retention.

claims.claim: Table 4 values increase with discounting and decrease with releases under constant price.
claims.assessment: All 12 native cells preserve these ordinal trends. Native model not reproduced by two disclosed initial-cohort timing assumptions.

claims.claim: Temporary value loss almost negligible when release rates are small and credit generation unrestricted.
claims.assessment: Conditional economic statement; no measured rate or permanence factor. Native 1% release/1% discount cell 48.5% demonstrates scope of the qualification.

claims.claim: Economic compensation applies across all six cases when some party remains liable.
claims.assessment: Accounting-party reconstruction is not proof of enforcement, solvency or actual collection.

claims.claim: Increasing permanent-credit prices preserve the general tendency.
claims.assessment: Price path and convergence conditions omitted. Analyst examples show growing replacement costs and divergence for some paths; no blanket native-error claim.

claims.claim: Historical credit periods max 21 years energy and 60 forestry, with 10/30 alternatives.
claims.assessment: Footnote 26 seven/twenty years plus two renewals gives stated maxima; historical instruments not reverified.

claims.claim: Expiry of temporary credits acts financially like releasing all surviving carbon at credit-period end.
claims.assessment: Accounting equivalence, explicitly possible continued physical storage; no physical release inferred.

claims.claim: Short 20–60 year crediting periods can reduce CCS CDM attractiveness.
claims.assessment: Synthetic finite-expiry examples support the mechanism, not the authors numeric model or current project profitability.

claims.claim: Figure 2 illustrates missed value after crediting ends for 0/1/5/10% release paths.
claims.assessment: Schematic/unscaled plot; release normalization and time law not identified from line shape.

claims.claim: Capture does not prevent CO2 formation, and accounting must include later releases.
claims.assessment: Applies to discussed point-source framing; biomass caveat remains, no whole-chain LCA result.

claims.claim: Release rates as small as widely suggested (>0.01) make replacement costs almost negligible.
claims.assessment: Literal greater-than sign and missing unit preserved as unresolved notation; no corrected<0.01% assumed.

claims.claim: Shared stores, several exporters, stock-dependent releases and transboundary reservoirs complicate accounting.
claims.assessment: Explicit limitation; fixed six-case taxonomy does not solve commingled allocation or multi-country plume liability.

claims.claim: Future targets for non-Annex countries may change allocation.
claims.assessment: Historical policy uncertainty, not a 2026 national-target classification.

claims.claim: Complete accurate accounting and long-term liability are necessary for credibility.
claims.assessment: Author conclusion/recommendation, not demonstrated legal enforcement or retained-carbon guarantee.

claims.claim: Bibliography, report identities and source spellings underpin the evidence chain.
claims.assessment: All 38 native entries read, none verified against exact originals; placeholder Pearce identifiers and author/year ambiguities remain open.

claims.claim: No separately retained supplement, code or explicit availability statement identified.
claims.assessment: No online absence inferred; external retrieval paused pending requested Chrome connection.

claims.claim: Paper 1 must separate financial credit value/expiry, physical retention and net avoided mass.
claims.assessment: 39 limited checks and disclosed models add no native pressure-constrained annual service, complete capture-to-ship inventory or accepted operating/GHG input.
